record.goal: The PreToolUse guard core: every tool call reduces to a set of effects and is denied when its effects leave the task's granted set. Only a small closed table of rows yields effects other than top; every form outside the table is top and denied. Later specs add rows, never this one
out: Jev or any model in the guard path
Judging whether text a tool returns contains instructions
Sandboxing or host execution policy
Restricting reads
Removing the existing `enforce.deny` declarations from wiki pages

Rows beyond the core table. Three follow-up specs add them after this one merges: git and gh writes and network (continuations, per-call configuration, worktree operations, host aliases); PowerShell and cmd (providers, parameter prefixes, members, copy and link cmdlets); shell semantics (directory changes inside groups and loops, traps, awk, archives, links, curl). Until then those commands are denied in app-managed sessions
done: python -m ruff check tool laya

`tool/guard.py` (with `guard_models.py`, `guard_windows.py`, `guard_grant.py`) parses a Bash or PowerShell command into a tree covering `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `$(...)`, backticks, redirections and nested shell strings (`bash -c`, `sh -c`, `pwsh -Command`, `powershell -Command`, `cmd /c`) recursed to a fixed depth, and reduces the tree to effects: read, write(path), delete(path), spawn(executable), network(host), and top for anything undecidable such as `eval`, `-EncodedCommand`, a variable or glob in a write path, an unclosed quote or substitution, or depth exhausted

The closed table in `guard_models.py` holds only these rows, each with the flags it understands: read-only listing, reading and searching programs on both hosts (for example `ls`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `grep`, `rg`, `find` without actions, `diff`, `echo`, `pwd`, `Get-Content`, `Get-ChildItem`, `Select-String`, `Test-Path`); the adapter's gate, verification and registered check commands matched as exact commands; git `status`, `diff`, `log`, `show`, `rev-parse`, `add <paths>`, `commit -m`/`-F` and `push` with at most a remote and a branch, none of them with `-c`, `-C`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `--exec-path` or a config, alias, worktree or submodule verb; and plain `>`/`>>` redirection to a literal path. Every other program, flag or construct reduces to top, including every PowerShell cmdlet and member not in the read-only rows, gh, curl, archives, links, `cd` anywhere but the first statement, `trap`, `awk`, loops and functions

Review scope: a form outside the table that reduces to top and is denied is the intended outcome, not a finding. A finding is a table row whose effects miss a real effect, a form that reaches a row it should not, a grant or containment error, or a crash or performance failure
Path-state tracking is bounded: when the number of distinct directory states exceeds a fixed limit the call reduces to top, so the guard's work grows at most linearly with the command

The grant for a task is computed once per call from the worktree root (only the spec's artifact root when the profile is plan), the temporary directories and the session's memory folder, the adapter's gate, verification commands and registered checks, the search command, git and gh verbs with their write targets and the git remotes' hosts, and an optional adapter `[guard]` table that declares extra write roots, network hosts and executables but never a command pattern; `.git`, `.claude`, `.codex`, `.wiki/adapter.toml` and `verification.toml` are never granted

A Bash call is denied exactly when its effect set is not contained in the grant, and an Edit, Write, MultiEdit or apply_patch call is denied when its resolved target lies outside the write roots; every denial names the offending effect and path and the grant that would allow it; the guard judges only app-managed sessions (`WIKI_AGENT_MANAGED=1`) in a checkout with an adapter, and tools that neither run a shell nor edit a file count as reads

The guard runs on both hosts: wired through `apply.py`'s pretooluse path for Claude and chained in `codex_pretool.py` for Codex, after the existing `host_boundary` and declared deny checks, which keep their current behaviour

Property tests pin: monotonicity over complete commands (appending tokens never removes an effect, top absorbing), nested-shell recursion, top on the undecidable forms, containment on Windows and POSIX paths including `..`, junctions and drive-letter forms, and fail-open on any exception with UTF-8 pinned

A corpus of at least two hundred real commands taken from session records (raw/actions holds no shell commands) has expected effects recorded in `eval/guard/corpus.json`; the test asserts the derived effects match and that the guard answers each call under 200 ms on this machine

`docs/hooks-setup.md` documents the grant table and the denial message, and `deny.py`'s ponytail note about nested shells that the check did not follow is removed, because nested shells are now checked

record.goal: A spec record can carry a versioned requirements section with ids, grounds, decision status and verification items, from which the human review document and the task-specific agent input are rendered by code from one frozen snapshot, behind a setting that defaults off and leaves today's agent input byte-identical

The spec block accepted by `specs.fields` takes an optional `requirements` list; each item has `id` (R1, R2, …), `text`, `source` in {original, policy, repository, decision} with a locator, and `status` in {confirmed, assumed, undecided, not_applicable}; optional `preconditions`, `postconditions`, `invariants`, `failures`, `depends_on`, `context` (paths), `verify` (items with expected result) and `global: true`; unknown keys and ids not unique or referenced but undefined are refused with a named error, and `tool/prompts/next-task.md` documents the field

The original request text is stored verbatim in `original` and never altered by any save, edit, revise or spec-update path; `REVISABLE` excludes `original`, `requirements[].source` and verification results, and a test proves each path leaves them untouched

The record carries `spec_version` (an integer that increments whenever `requirements` change) and `spec_digest` (sha256 of the canonical requirements JSON); a test shows an edit of a requirement bumps both and an edit of `goal` alone does not

`specs.human(spec)` renders Markdown with purpose, behaviour, constraints, each requirement with its id, source, status and verification items, the undecided items and conflicts listed, and original text shown as original; `specs.agent(spec, task=None)` renders the structured input holding the selected requirements, every `global: true` requirement, the contracts of each `depends_on` target, context paths and verify items, with omitted requirements listed by id as available on request

`specs.equivalent(human_md, agent_json)` reports every requirement id, status, condition, negation, unit and verify item present in one rendering and missing in the other; a test mutates each rendering and shows the difference is caught, and a test over the fixture specs shows two renderings of the same snapshot are equivalent
A test shows `specs.agent` with a task selection that would drop a `global` requirement or a `depends_on` contract fails with the missing ids named, never silently

With the setting `SPEC_VIEWS=on` in the hub `.env` (default off, read through `common.settings.pick`), `specs.system` carries the agent view plus `spec_version` and `spec_digest`; with it off, `specs.brief` output is byte-identical to the current output on the ten saved records under `raw/specs/wiki-agent/`

At the first work turn with the setting on, the server compares the prompt's `spec_version` with the saved record and rebuilds the session when they differ; a test shows a stale prompt is refreshed before the turn and an equal one is reused

A requirement whose `depends_on` target is `undecided` makes the first turn hold with the blocking id named and ask the person; a spec whose undecided items are not depended on starts normally, and a test covers both

Verification results are stored outside the spec record under `raw/specs/<repo>/<id>.verify.json`, keyed by requirement id, `spec_version` and `spec_digest`, written only by the server's gate path; a result recorded under a previous version is reported as stale, not as a pass, and a test proves it

`GET /api/specs/{id}/views` returns `{human, agent, spec_version, spec_digest}` and the spec card shows the human document in a collapsible section when the record has requirements; the browser check opens a card with requirements and sees the ids rendered

Documented in `docs/plans/loop/3-spec.md` under a new section naming the data model, the two renderers, the setting, the version and undecided behaviour, with assumptions and undecided design points listed as such
